title: Republic Airways® Plane Pull 2026 Recap
summary: The 2026 Republic Airways® Plane Pull presented by Lucas Oil marked the 14th time we’ve gathered together with our community to raise funds and awareness for charities whose mission is to support and grant hope to children suffering from life-threat…
body_text: The 2026 Republic Airways® Plane Pull presented by Lucas Oil marked the 14th time we’ve gathered together with our community to raise funds and awareness for charities whose mission is to support and grant hope to children suffering from life-threatening or terminal illness. The Plane Pull began as a celebration of Tyler Frenzel, a 9-year-old boy from Carmel, IN, who passed away from leukemia in 2004. Many of the organizations we champion today supported Tyler during his treatment. What started as a grassroots giving movement founded by our Associates has grown into an annual commemoration of what we can accomplish together. BEST Principles in Action At Republic Airways, we know we can’t succeed without the support of our communities. Dedication to our BEST Guiding Principles drives us to give back and provide our Associates the opportunity to engage with causes they care about. B e good stewards of our resources E ncourage a culture of fun and action S trive for excellence in everything we do T rust, respect and care for one another The 2026 Plane Pull is an excellent example of one of the many ways our BEST Guiding Principles come to life through the passion of our Associates and our community. 2026 Plane Pull by the Numbers “Thank you to everybody for coming out and making this the best plane pull yet.” — Republic Airways President and Chief Commercial Officer Matt Koscal This year’s Plane Pull saw 52 teams participate, and combined with the 345 guests at the Plane Pull Gala at the Lucas Oil Estate, raised over $850,000 for A Kid Again, Indiana Wish, Peyton Manning Children’s Hospital, Riley Children’s Foundation and several other children-focused charities. This figure brings the 14-year total to nearly $7 million. An extraordinary number that is only possible thanks to our Associates, beneficiaries, partners, community members and especially our sponsors. Looking Forward to Next Year Want to support your community? Mark your calendars for Saturday, April 24, 2027, when we’ll celebrate the 15th Annual Plane Pull and continue this tradition of giving. In the meantime, learn about all the other ways Republic Airways serves causes across the country and even abroad .

title: Unlayer Enterprise: Your Guide to Embeddable Tech at Scale
summary: An in-depth Enterprise-focused overview of choosing an embeddable builder built for compliant workflows, flexible deployment, & fast team-wide content creation.
body_text: Enterprises today operate in a world where speed, personalization, governance, and security are the backbone of every customer-facing experience. Whether you’re running a marketing automation platform, a CRM, an eCommerce suite, or an all-in-one SaaS, the customer expects polished, on-brand, accessible, and dynamic content without ever touching code. And while creating content is easy, creating it at scale, across teams, within shared systems, and without breaking brand rules is incredibly hard, especially if you’re trying to build your own content editor or rely on fragmented open-source tools. This is exactly where Unlayer Enterprise comes in. Unlayer isn’t just an email or page editor. It’s a fully embeddable, enterprise-grade content creation platform built specifically for companies that need: Full control over security, compliance, and deployment A scalable editor embedded directly into their product A white-label, brandable, no-code content experience Flexible APIs and SDKs for deep customization Strong governance: SSO, RBAC, audit logs, accessibility Reliability, uptime guarantees, and global infrastructure Enterprise support, SLAs, and dedicated onboarding This guide provides everything you need to understand Unlayer Enterprise, including its comparison to Unlayer self-serve plans and open-source editors, its ability to enable scalable no-code experiences, and when teams should consider upgrading. 1. Why Enterprise Content Creation Needs More Than Just an Editor Enterprise content operations are more complex than simply creating emails or landing pages. Large organizations must balance: Faster campaign production Brand consistency across global teams Regulatory and security demands Developer-friendly integrations Accessibility compliance Reliable performance at scale Unlayer Enterprise solves this by combining white-label flexibility, on-premise control, enterprise-grade security, and an API-first embedding model tailored for high-growth, regulated, or distributed organizations. The core challenges enterprises face today Challenges Explanation Strict Compliance Requirements Industries such as healthcare, finance, and government have strict rules governing where data resides, who can access it, and how it’s stored. Cloud-only platforms often fall short, forcing enterprises to seek full control over their data. Heightened Security Risks Data breaches and regulatory fines are costly . Enterprises must secure sensitive customer and business data with robust systems, not consumer-level protections. Accessibility Obligations Modern organizations must ensure content is accessible under WCAG and VPAT standards, which many traditional editors cannot guarantee. Brand Dilution Across Teams Distributed marketing teams often create inconsistent visuals and messaging due to a lack of centralized brand controls. Unstructured Collaboration & Approval Chaos Without structured roles and checks, enterprises experience content errors, version conflicts, and time-consuming revisions. Authentication Friction Multiple logins across various tools create unnecessary complexity and introduce security vulnerabilities. Scaling Limitations Growing volumes of emails, pages, and assets can strain systems not built for enterprise-level throughput. Disconnected Tech Stacks Tools that don’t integrate with existing CRMs, workflows, or automation platforms lead to manual processes and operational inefficiencies. Lack of Visibility & Reporting Enterprise leaders require in-depth analytics to comprehend usage, compliance, and ROI across multiple regions. Minimal Support for Large Teams Enterprise adoption requires assistance with migration, custom SLAs, consulting, and proactive support, not just a ticketing system. What makes Unlayer truly enterprise-ready This section outlines the most critical enterprise-grade features. 🔍 Full feature breakdown in the original post: Unlayer for Enterprise: White-Label, Secure, & Built to Embed 1. On-premise deployment Unlayer offers an on-premise deployment option, allowing enterprises to host the editor on their internal infrastructure. Why this matters Ensures data residency and compliance Enables custom authentication, monitoring, and internal policies Supports industries where cloud SaaS alone is not allowed This provides enterprises with consumer-grade ease while maintaining enterprise-level governance. 2. Enterprise-grade security & compliance Unlayer is SOC 2 Type II certified, GDPR compliant, and offers a full suite of protective measures. Key safeguards Data encryption Audit logs Vulnerability scans Backup & recovery DDoS protection Network security Granular access controls 3. Accessibility compliance (WCAG + VPAT) Unlayer meets WCAG 2.1 standards and provides VPAT documentation, helping enterprises: Achieve accessibility compliance Deliver inclusive digital communications Avoid legal or institutional accessibility violations 4. White-label capabilities Unlayer can be white-labeled down to: Logos UI elements Custom domains Theme and layout 5. Deep customization Unlayer can be extended with custom tools , custom property editors, and tailored UI behaviors such as appearance , editor behavior , and content settings . Related: The Dev’s Guide to Customizing and Extending Editor SDKs 6. Role-Based Access Controls (RBAC) Unlayer sets clear boundaries for teams through enterprise-level RBAC . Benefits Prevents overwrites and errors Establishes clear ownership Smoothens approval chains Scales collaboration safely RBAC ensures large teams collaborate efficiently without sacrificing control. 7. Single Sign-On (SSO) Unlayer supports: SAML OAuth Custom authentication flows 8. Scalability & high performance Unlayer is engineered for enterprises that produce high volumes of content. Distributed infrastructure Global CDN 99.99% uptime SLA Marketing teams across regions can work without performance slowdowns. 9. Embedded, API-first integration Unlayer embeds seamlessly into any product and integrates with major frameworks. Developer benefits Native feel inside your app Flexible JavaScript SDK and plugins ( React , Angular , & Vue ) Deep API customization 10. Advanced analytics & reporting Unlayer provides insights on: Template usage Editor activity Team performance Version history Workflow efficiency These insights help enterprises streamline their processes and identify areas of friction. 11. Enterprise support & services Unlayer offers white-glove enterprise support, such as: 24/7 priority support SLA-backed guarantees Dedicated CSM + Technical Account Manager Custom onboarding Migration assistance Training sessions Developer and admin documentation In short, Unlayer isn’t just a tool; it’s a long-term technology partner. 2. Unlayer Enterprise vs Self-Serve – Key Differences Why this comparison matters for growth & scale Many businesses, especially SaaS companies, face a significant decision: start with a lightweight, pay-as-you-go editor or invest in a full, enterprise-grade solution from the outset. For growing teams, the choice influences not only cost but also architecture, compliance, customization, and the long-term developer burden. Unlayer’s “ Enterprise vs Self-Serve plans ” article breaks down when it's better to stay lean and when it's worth moving up to Enterprise. What are the self-serve plans? Unlayer offers three self-serve plans, namely Launch, Scale, and Optimize . Core features of self-serve plans Drag-and-Drop Editor: All self-serve tiers include the core no-code drag-and-drop builder for creating emails , landing pages , popups , and more. SDKs & APIs : Even self-serve customers can embed and integrate via JavaScript SDKs and REST APIs. Customization: Includes standard theming, blocks, and tools to customize the editor experience. Templates: Comes with pre-built templates that help speed up design work. Flexible, Pay-as-you-Go: These plans are ideal for teams that want to scale quickly without committing to a deeply custom setup. Typical use cases for self-serve plans Unlayer’s self-serve plans are well-suited for: 📈 Startups — Testing new SaaS ideas or validating builder integrations. 📈 Small / Mid-sized Businesses (SMBs) — Wanting a cost-effective builder without heavy customization overhead. 📈 Teams prioritizing speed to market — They may not need heavy compliance or deployment options. What does the Enterprise plan offer? This is where the article dives into why and how the Enterprise plan is a different, more powerful offering. Enterprise-grade features beyond self-serve Security & Compliance: SOC 2 certification, GDPR support, uptime SLA, and audit logs. Deep Customization: White-labeling with brand style guides . Custom OpenAI connectors, server-side rendering, custom exporters, and multi-language template support. Flexible Deployment Options: Support for private cloud, on-premise, or offline deployments, not just standard cloud. Advanced Workflows: Early access to new features, delayed release controls (control when new features are enabled), and more customizable infrastructure via API-first design. Support & Services: Priority customer support, a dedicated Customer Success Manager (CSM), technical consulting, migration help, and custom SLAs. Who typically chooses the Enterprise plan Enterprise is most relevant for: Large SaaS companies building their own content tooling Regulated industries (finance, healthcare, etc.) that need compliance and control High-growth platforms that require heavy customization, SLAs, and governance Feature-by-feature comparison Here’s a clear comparison table of how Self-Serve vs Enterprise differ along key dimensions. Category Self-Serve (Launch / Scale / Optimize) Enterprise Security & Compliance Baseline protections, but no SLA Full SOC 2, GDPR, custom agreements, SLA, continuity guarantee Brand / UI Control White-labeling, themes, custom CSS Everything in self-serve + full style guide, brand control, exporter customizations Customization & Integration SDKs + APIs, but limited custom tools Unlimited custom tools, custom exporters, SSR, OpenAI connector, deep integrations Content Builders Editors for email, page, popup, document Same builders + multi-language, content auditing, delayed release, early feature access Deployment Options Only cloud-hosted Cloud or on-premise/ offline/private cloud Access & Governance Basic user roles, team collaboration Unlimited users, role-based controls, SSO, full governance Support & Services Standard support (tickets, docs) Dedicated CSM, priority response, migration & training Analytics & Reporting Basic usage tracking Advanced analytics, detailed audit logs, custom validators, API integration 3. Why Scalability & Performance Matter for Enterprises At an enterprise scale, every tool must strike a balance between performance, reliability, and security. Traditional WYSIWYG editors often falter under enterprise demands because they lack the infrastructure, governance, and integration depth required. Unlayer is purpose-built to embed, customize, and govern a powerful design tool without overwhelming development teams. Major pain points for enterprises & how Unlayer addresses them 1. Scalability & reliability The pain point Need to support thousands of concurrent users, design edits, API calls, and campaign sends. ➡️ If the system is slow or unreliable: Designers can’t save or publish. Marketers are blocked, hurting campaign velocity. Customer support and operations suffer. ➡️ Performance issues damage brand trust; downtime can lead to revenue loss. ➡️ For global teams, consistency and low latency across regions are essential. Unlayer’s solution Distributed infrastructure + global CDN: ensures fast load times everywhere. 99.9% uptime SLA: gives enterprises confidence in reliability under load. Whether embedded across tenants or used in a single app, performance remains consistent. 2. Security, compliance & governance The pain point Enterprises are bound by strict regulatory frameworks (e.g., GDPR, SOC 2, HIPAA). Without proper controls, risks include data breaches, regulatory fines, and a lack of accountability. Traditional editors often lack fine-grained access control or auditability. Unlayer’s solution SOC 2 Type II certification and GDPR compliance built in. Encryption for data in transit and at rest. Security features: DDoS protection, vulnerability scanning, backup & recovery. Governance: RBAC, audit logs, and Single Sign-On (SSO) via SAML and OAuth. 3. Deep integration & customization The pain point Enterprise stacks rarely use a single platform, as they often include CRMs (such as Salesforce or HubSpot), marketing platforms, and in-house applications. Without seamless integration, teams waste time on manual syncing and suffer from fragmented workflows. Many editors force you into rigid templates or workflows, which can limit brand fidelity and UX flexibility. Unlayer’s solution API-first architecture + embedded editor: Use JavaScript SDK and plugins for React, Angular, or Vue. Custom UI & Branding: The editor’s look and behavior can be tailored to precisely match your platform. Custom Tools & Extensions: Developers can build bespoke editor tools aligned with enterprise workflows. Dynamic Content Support: Personalize designs with event-driven or user-specific data (e.g., names, locations, offers). Full Template API: Load, save , export designs via REST, making automation and content flows easier. Third-Party Ecosystem: Integrate with CRMs, email automation platforms , and other systems via connectors or webhooks. Multi-Tenant Support: Run multiple Unlayer instances under one umbrella, ideal for platforms serving many brands. 4. Operational efficiency & reducing developer overhead The pain point Building an in-house email editor becomes a maintenance nightmare. Engineers spend months on core functionality (drag/drop, responsive layout). Every browser or email-client update triggers new bugs or regressions. Dedicated QA and support are required just to keep the editor running. Engineering time is diverted from product innovation to maintenance. Unlayer’s solution Fast Embedding: Unlayer can be embedded in days, drastically reducing development cycles (up to 80% faster). Lower Developer Burden: Unlayer handles ongoing maintenance, browser compatibility, and feature updates. Constant Compatibility: Regular platform updates ensure seamless operation across devices and email clients. Enterprise Support: Dedicated onboarding, migration help, training, and SLA-backed support. Reliable at Scale: With a global CDN and guaranteed 99.99% uptime, Unlayer stays performant even under heavy load. 🔍 Deep Dive: Unlayer: A Scalable Builder for Enterprise-Level Performance 4. Why Security & Compliance Are Mission-Critical for Modern Enterprises In 2025, data breaches continue to expose nearly 94 million records worldwide, and enterprises using content tools need more than convenience; they require ironclad security, regulatory compliance, and auditability. For any platform handling sensitive user/customer data, especially in sectors such as healthcare, finance, or global SaaS, failing to meet compliance standards (like SOC 2, HIPAA, or GDPR) isn’t just risky; it can be a deal-breaker for partnerships, contracts, or enterprise adoption. Unlayer’s compliance credentials Let’s have a look at Unlayer’s compliance credentials: SOC 2 Type II certification Unlayer is certified under SOC 2 Type II, meaning its controls around security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy are audited and verified. That gives enterprises real assurance about data handling and operational safeguards, an important checkbox during audits or procurement. Supports HIPAA compliance for healthcare use cases For organizations handling Protected Health Information (PHI), Unlayer supports HIPAA-compliant workflows: end-to-end encryption, role-based access restrictions, audit trails, data isolation, and secure network protocols. This makes it viable for healthcare providers, patient-facing platforms, or any application needing strict confidentiality. GDPR compliance and privacy standards Unlayer supports GDPR requirements: secure storage, data minimization and purpose limitations, consent management, data access/portability, and audit logging. This helps enterprises cater to customers globally while remaining compliant with European (and other) data-protection regulations. What security & compliance mean in practice (Enterprise-grade controls) Unlayer doesn’t just claim compliance; it builds in the technical and operational controls enterprises need. Key safeguards include: Encryption — for data at rest and in transit, protecting sensitive content and user data. Granular Access Controls — role-based permissions ensure that only authorized users can access or modify sensitive data. Audit Logs & Activity Trails — every action is logged, enabling traceability, accountability, and compliance reporting. Network Security & Vulnerability Monitoring — regular scans, hardened infrastructure, DDoS protections, and security monitoring guard against external threats. Backup & Recovery Protocols — ensuring data integrity and recovery in case of failures, which is critical for enterprise reliability. Together, these features form a strong compliance backbone, enabling enterprise teams to meet internal and external regulatory requirements while still offering a flexible content creation tool. ✅ Unlayer Enterprise compliance & security checklist Here’s a table that can serve as a quick, scannable reference to decide if Unlayer meets your security, compliance, and governance needs. Unlayer Enterprise vs. Open-Source Editors: The Right Context for Choosing an Editor Before committing to a content/editing tool, enterprises often ask: “Should we build/embed our own, use open-source, or go for a managed enterprise solution?” This article helps answer that by comparing Unlayer Enterprise with several popular open-source editors on key dimensions like security, scalability, customization, support, and total cost of ownership. It lays out a decision framework, not just about features, but about organizational maturity, compliance demands, long-term maintenance, and risk tolerance. ✅ Strengths of Unlayer Enterprise (vs. Open-source) Here are the major advantages that Unlayer offers over typical open-source editors: Built-in Security & Compliance: Unlayer offers SOC 2 Type II compliance and GDPR support, which are rarely offered by open-source editors out of the box. Deployment Flexibility: Unlayer Enterprise supports private cloud, on-premises, and managed deployments, making compliance and data residency easier. Deep Embedding, White-Label & Developer-Focused Customization: Unlayer provides an API-first, SDK-based architecture, with plugins for embedding in React, Angular, and Vue frameworks. Developers get full control with custom blocks, exporters, UI behavior, custom tools, branding, and styling, enabling a polished, native feel inside your product. Scalability, Performance & Multi-User Governance: Built for enterprise-scale usage, such as high concurrency, large template libraries, many users, stable performance, and robust governance. Dedicated Support, Maintenance & Lower Long-Term Overhead: Unlayer offers dedicated support, Service-Level Agreements (SLAs), customer success managers, and maintenance, so you don’t rely on a community or internal developer resources. Predictable Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) at Scale: While open-source editors may seem free initially, their hidden costs , like maintenance, updates, bug fixes, compliance overhead, infrastructure, and support, often stack up. So, Unlayer Enterprise delivers better TCO for organizations that care about reliability, compliance, and scale. ⚠️ Where open-source editors still make sense Key advantages of open-source editors Cost Efficiency for Early-Stage or Lean Teams: No license fees; you pay mostly with developer time. Good for small projects, prototypes, or MVPs. Maximum Flexibility and Ownership: Full access to code, ability to heavily customize or fork, and no vendor lock-in. Great if you have a strong engineering team comfortable with maintenance. Faster Experimentation / Lower Commitment: For startups building fast, open-source editors allow you to iterate quickly without a long-term vendor contract. Trade-offs & hidden costs Lack of built-in compliance, security, and enterprise governance. Need for in-house infrastructure management, security maintenance, and updates. Absence of formal support can slow down bug fixes, security updates, or feature development. Risk of fragmented maintenance if the community slows down or abandons the project. 🧭 Decision matrix: What to use, when Here’s a simplified decision matrix crafted for teams evaluating editors: Your Context / Need Recommended Early-stage startup, small team, limited compliance needs, fast prototyping Open-Source Editor (e.g., GrapesJS, Easy-Email, etc.) Lean SMB needing basic email or landing-page builder, with minimal infrastructure burden Open-Source or Self-Serve editor SaaS platform expecting growth, multiple teams/users, or multi-tenant architecture, but limited internal maintenance bandwidth Unlayer Enterprise Regulated industry (finance, health, enterprise contracts) needing compliance, auditability, and data residency Unlayer Enterprise Need for embedding editor inside product, with branding & white-labeling, consistent UX Unlayer Enterprise Large organizations with global teams, need for uptime SLA, multi-user governance, and robust support Unlayer Enterprise In short, the choice isn’t about which editor is best, but about which editor best fits your organization’s scale, risk tolerance, and growth plans. 6. When to Upgrade Your Unlayer Plan — What to Watch Out For Now, let’s help teams, especially SaaS products and growing platforms, decide when it makes sense to move up the tiers of Unlayer — from Free → Self-Serve → Enterprise — based on their growth, needs, and maturity. The below summary frames upgrade decisions as strategic inflection points, not just optional feature checks. Overview of Unlayer plans & what they unlock Free / Forever Free — Basic access: core builders (email, page, popup, document). Best for early-stage projects or MVPs. Self-Serve Paid Plans: Launch (~ US$250/month) — Adds white-labeling, cloud API, storage, custom tools, brand/UI control, custom storage , and basic embed/integration tools. Scale (~ US$750/month) — Adds collaboration features, custom blocks, audit tools, team workflows, custom image libraries , smart merge tags , and theme support. Optimize (~ US$2,000/month) — Further unlocks advanced features, including custom themes & CSS , synced blocks , AMP support, inbox previews , and deeper customization, making it ideal for high-volume and complex use cases. Enterprise (Custom Plan) — Tailored to large organizations. Includes everything from Optimize plus enterprise-grade security/compliance, on-premise or private-cloud deployment, custom integrations, multi-language/template support, SLAs, and dedicated support. This tiered structure provides you with a clear growth path : start lean, and upgrade when your needs evolve. Key signals that it’s time to upgrade Before we get into the details, this overview will help you understand exactly when it’s time to move up, based on real indicators. 1. Growth in team size & collaboration needs When your content operations move beyond a solo or small team, and you start adding designers, marketers, and developers to your growing team, coordination becomes critical. Upgrading adds support for team collaboration, role-based permissions, auditability, and shared workflows, reducing chaos caused by concurrent edits or version conflicts. 2. Branding & UI/UX consistency needs If you want the editor experience to feel native to your product (custom branding, UI control, custom themes/CSS), especially when exposing the editor to external users, self-serve may fall short. Higher tiers enable full white labeling, theme control, custom domains, and editor customization, providing stronger brand cohesion. 3. Integration & extensibility requirements As products mature, embedding the editor deeply into workflows (APIs, custom tools, export pipelines, automation) becomes crucial. Upgrading allows for custom tools, custom storage, advanced exporter or API usage, enabling the editor to fit your architecture rather than forcing you to adapt. 4. Security, compliance & deployment constraints Some organizations or clients may require private cloud or on-premise deployments, as well as data governance and compliance protocols that go beyond what self-serve can handle. The Enterprise plan addresses these with enterprise-grade deployment options, compliance support, and infrastructure tailored for regulated or sensitive environments. 5. Content volume, complexity & multi-brand / multi-tenant needs When content workload increases, many templates, frequent campaigns, multilingual content, or multi-tenant usage can strain basic plans due to complexity. Higher tiers support advanced features, including synced blocks, custom themes/CSS, multi-brand management, enhanced QA (previews and inbox previews), and workflow controls that scale. 6. Expectation for support, SLAs & long-term stability Growing teams often require guaranteed uptime, support response SLAs, migration assistance, or customer success services. Enterprise plan offers dedicated support, custom agreements, and peace of mind as usage scales. Risks of upgrading (Or delaying upgrade) Timing matters because upgrading too early or too late both carries trade-offs. Here’s how: 🚦Risk of upgrading too early Paying for features you don’t need yet means wasted budget. Unused customization or collaboration features. Potential distraction from core product development. 🧩 Risk of delaying the upgrade too long Constraints on team productivity result in design bottlenecks, and collaboration suffers. Brand inconsistency and a poor user experience if the editor feels tacked on. Increased technical debt: retrofitting integrations, redoing workflows, migrating templates when scale hits. 🔍 Deep Dive: From Startup to Enterprise: When to Upgrade Your Unlayer Plan Decision guide — which plan fits which stage Based on team size, usage, and needs, the following are the typical scenarios in which each plan is most suitable. Stage / Scenario Recommended Plan Solo developer / early-stage prototype / MVP Free — cost-free, minimal commitment, simple builder access Small team with basic branding/embed needs Launch — white-labeling, branding, custom tools, embed + basic integration/features Growing team, collaboration across roles, multiple templates, or small teams Scale — collaboration tools, team workflows, custom blocks, auditability High volume content, needs for design governance, QA, sophisticated workflows Optimize — advanced customization, synced blocks, previews, multi-brand support SaaS platform or enterprise-grade needs: compliance, multi-tenant, integrations, long-term support Enterprise — full infrastructure flexibility, compliance, SLAs, advanced integration, white-labeling & customization 7. What Makes Unlayer Enterprise’s No-Code Editor Stand Out Large organizations quickly outgrow generic no-code tools because such tools often lack governance, branding control, deep integration, and flexibility. Unlayer Enterprise offers a no-code editor , but with an architecture built for scalability, control, and customization, so enterprises don’t have to sacrifice robustness for ease of use. Key pillars of Unlayer’s no-code offering Instead of a standalone tool, Unlayer can be embedded directly within your application to create emails, landing pages, popups, and documents. The editor is API-first. Through its SDK and plugins, developers can embed the editor in React, Angular, or Vue applications and customize its behavior. Developers can build custom tools and blocks, extend functionality, integrate with CRMs, ESPs, automation systems, and connect editor workflows to backend systems. The API also enables load, save, and export workflows for formats like HTML, image, document, and ZIP, making content generation automatable and flexible. You can fully brand the editor: logos, color schemes, UI layout, domain, etc., so the editor feels native to your product rather than a third-party addon. Developers can predefine brand-approved blocks ( headers , footers , buttons , etc.) that marketers/designers can drag and drop freely. The editor supports user roles and permissions, allowing granular control over who can create, edit, manage templates, or publish content. Advanced analytics & usage reporting You can integrate any analytics tool into your platform along with Unlayer, which delivers audit logs showing who did what, which templates are used, performance metrics, and content usage patterns. This visibility helps teams enforce brand standards, monitor adoption, identify bottlenecks, and optimize workflows across departments. What unlayer enterprise’s no-code editor enables for SAAS/Products/Large teams Branded, seamless editing experience inside your product — making content creation feel native to your platform rather than an external tool. Easy content creation for non-technical users while preserving design governance and code-quality controls. Flexible integrations with backend workflows, CRMs, ESPs, and automation systems, enabling dynamic content, personalization, and export workflows. Scalable collaboration and governance — multiple teams contributing content, with control over roles, permissions, and auditability. Reliable, secure, compliant infrastructure — enabling enterprises to offer no-code content creation for users/customers, even under strict compliance or data-residency requirements. Faster time to market — no need to build an editor from scratch; embed Unlayer to immediately offer email, landing-page, popup, or document editing features in your product. Read More: How Unlayer Enterprise Powers Customizable No-Code Experiences 8. Embedding Unlayer into Your Product – The Integration Blueprint To make it easier for you, this section explains how to embed Unlayer into your enterprise stack and includes a link to a detailed guide where you can explore the full process, best practices, and technical considerations. Pre-embedding checklist — what to plan before you start Before you drop in the editor, it’s wise to run a quick health check of your architecture. 1️⃣ Decide on deployment & compliance requirements If compliance or data residency matters → pick on-premise. If you want speed and minimal setup → cloud embed. 2️⃣ Choose which builder modes you need Unlayer supports multiple builder modes: email, page, popup, and document. You can embed one or more depending on your product’s use cases. 3️⃣ Plan storage & asset handling (For on-premise) You need storage/hosting for custom blocks, user uploads, font files, and assets. Decide whether to serve assets via CDN or internal hosting (depending on compliance/performance needs). 4️⃣ Set up security, permissions & domain controls before launch If using enterprise features: configure role-based access, SSO, domain allowlists, and audit logging. For multi-tenant/multi-brand platforms: plan template ownership, block permissions, and design/version access. Embed modes — Cloud (SaaS) vs on-premise Before integrating, you choose one of two deployment paths, depending on your requirements. Cloud / SaaS embed Fastest path: include Unlayer’s hosted script, initialize the editor, and let Unlayer handle hosting, scaling, and updates. Great for teams who prioritize speed-to-market and don’t need strict infrastructure control. On-premise / Self-hosted embed All assets, including editor bundle, custom blocks, fonts, and user uploads, live on your own servers or CDN. Ideal for organizations with strict compliance, data residency, or internal security policies. Provides full control over storage, block assets, uploads, and infrastructure, ideal for regulated industries or firms with strict governance requirements. 🔍 For a detailed, step-by-step integration workflow, including configuration, deployment, and recommended practices, refer to the full guide here: Embed Unlayer Into Your Enterprise Stack . What integration enables for large enterprises ⚡ Fully embedded editor experience: Users design emails, pages, popups, and documents inside your application, without ever leaving the app . ⚡ Unified branding and UX: Editor can be themed and styled to match your platform, giving a seamless, native feel. ⚡ Flexible template and content management: Templates saved as JSON → easy versioning, reuse across accounts/tenants, export as HTML/other formats. ⚡ Dynamic content & personalization readiness: Merge tags, dynamic placeholders, and customizable data injection make the editor powerful for SaaS, marketing, and user-personalization flows. ⚡ Scalable collaboration and maintenance: Because Unlayer is maintained by its team (or self-hosted), you avoid the continuous burden of building, updating, and fixing a custom editor, saving developer and QA time. When embedding makes the most sense: use cases & contexts Embed Unlayer when: 🧩 You run a SaaS platform, CRM, or marketing tool, and want to provide content creation inside your product UI. 🧩 You need to offer email, page, popup, or document builders without building them from scratch. 🧩 You want to maintain strict control over branding, compliance, and data residency (on-premise embed). 🧩 You aim for fast time-to-market, avoiding months of custom editor development. 🧩 You need template versioning, user workflows, multi-tenant support, and custom asset storage management for a large user base. To Wrap This All Up… Enterprises today need tools that keep pace with their scale, structure, and evolving digital needs. Across this guide, we’ve mapped out how Unlayer fits into that landscape and how teams can adopt it with clarity and confidence. What matters most is choosing a system that supports long-term growth, aligns with internal workflows, and reduces friction, rather than adding to it. For organizations evaluating their next step in modern content operations, Unlayer provides a dependable path forward and the flexibility to build exactly what your teams need. It’s a practical, future-ready choice for anyone seeking an enterprise content builder that seamlessly integrates into complex environments. Ready to Explore What Unlayer Can Do for Your Enterprise? 👉 Contact Sales to get started . FAQs 1. How long does it typically take for an enterprise to fully implement Unlayer? Implementation timelines vary based on your tech stack and deployment choice, but most enterprises complete initial setup, embedding the editor, configuring access, and aligning branding, within a few weeks. More complex cases, such as multi-environment rollouts or heavy customizations, may require slight extensions, but Unlayer’s team provides guidance to keep the process efficient. 2. Can Unlayer be adopted gradually instead of deploying it across all teams at once? Yes. Many organizations start with a single department or specific product area and expand once workflows are validated. Unlayer supports phased adoption, allowing teams to introduce the editor in controlled stages without disrupting existing systems. 3. What level of customization is possible without modifying the underlying codebase? Enterprises can adjust UI styling, add custom tools, configure behavior settings, and tailor the editing experience extensively through the SDK, without requiring any core code changes. This enables developers to tailor the editor to their unique business processes without compromising stability or upgradability. 4. How does Unlayer handle version updates without disrupting enterprise environments? Unlayer offers the ability to lock the builder to a specific version via version management . Enterprises can choose when to adopt new releases, and early-access channels are available for testing. This ensures that editor improvements never interfere with live workflows or customer-facing systems. 5. What kind of long-term support can enterprises expect beyond initial onboarding? Beyond setup, enterprises receive continuous assistance through strategic guidance, integration best practices, and periodic optimization reviews. Unlayer’s support teams stay involved to help organizations refine usage, accommodate new requirements, and evolve their implementation as business needs change. title: Batteries help detect water leaks to stop commercial property damage
summary: Water leaks are the main cause of property damage in commercial buildings. It is essential to have reliably powered smart meters and water leak detectors.
body_text: A recent article in Environmental Protection magazine reports that ‘Internal water leaks are the number one cause of property damage in commercial buildings, surpassing fire, theft, and weather-related events combined’ and that ‘Water-damage deductibles of $100,000 to $200,000 are now common’. It is therefore essential to have reliably powered smart meters and water leak detectors that continuously look for signs of a leak. Power failure is not an option when it comes to devices that can save properties and lives, such as pipe-fitted leak detectors, portable leak detectors and smart meters. These are applications in which the battery manufacturer Ultralife Corporation specializes. The company started out as a detector battery manufacturer – over 30 years ago – and has sold over 100 million batteries containing its small and light Thin Cells® . Additionally, Ultralife’s engineers worked closely with metering manufacturers to develop the ER Generation X range of Lithium Thionyl Chloride cells. These robust batteries are made from 100% stainless steel, so do not rust, and the D-size bobbin cell variant has a leading capacity of 19Ah, reducing the need for replacement. Pipe-fitted leak detector batteries Pipe-fitted leak detectors are often permanently installed into commercial properties and can automatically shut down the water supply in the event of a leak. Although often powered by AC mains, they will utilize batteries if the pipes are in a remote location without wiring access, or where the detector communicates via wireless rather than cabling. Lithium Thionyl Chloride batteries are well-suited for use in remote applications, as they have a high energy density (exceeding 400Whr/Kg) that results in a long service life. Additionally, the high and stable operating voltage of Lithium Thionyl Chloride batteries provides consistent performance, maintaining the accuracy and reliability of data transmission over time. Portable leak detector batteries Alternatively, portable leak detectors are ideal as a temporary measure or when installing fixed sensors is not feasible (e.g., temporary setups, rented spaces, complex legacy piping). Small devices, measuring as thin as 1.5cm, they can easily be moved between offices and buildings. Additionally, using multiple portable leak detectors often works out much cheaper than equipping an entire facility with fixed sensors. If water around them reaches a certain level, an alarm will sound or a notification will be sent to a smartphone. Due to the small size of the device, many use Lithium Coin Cells but Ultralife Thin Cells® (containing Lithium Manganese Dioxide chemistry) offer significant advantages. With thicknesses as low as 1.1mm and an energy density of around 500Wh/l and 400Wh/Kg, compared to just 300Wh/l and 260Wh/Kg for the best lithium coin cells, Ultralife Thin Cells® are ideal for embedding into discreet devices. Not only are they available in many different shapes and sizes, they also offer high performance thanks to low resistance current collectors that help to deliver the high bursts of energy required for data transmission. Smart meter batteries In addition to both types of leak detectors, smart meters can show signs of a water leak by displaying spikes in water consumption. Fitted with advanced sensors, many smart meters monitor water consumption in real-time, allowing businesses to take corrective measures quickly. Most major energy suppliers offer a mobile app that displays the data collected by smart meters, allowing business customers to track their energy usage even when they are out of the office. All of this relies on the smart meter having a reliable power source that allows it to record or transmit data accurately. Even smart meters that are powered by AC mains will often integrate a battery in-case of AC mains failure. However, not all batteries are manufactured to the same standards and offer the same performance, so it is important that smart meter manufacturers undertake a thorough assessment. For example, Ultralife’s D size bobbin cell offers an industry leading capacity of 19Ah that helps it to be embedded for the lifetime of the device. Furthermore, by adding ultracapacitors as part of a battery system, Ultralife's D size cell can support the latest 5G-compatible smart meters that demand a periodic, high-power consumption. Water leak detectors and smart meters are only as effective as the batteries that power them. With water leaks now the leading cause of commercial property damage and insurance deductibles reaching six figures, having reliable water leak detectors and smart meters has never been more important.

title: Northpointe Bancshares, Inc. Announces Completion of $70 Million Subordinated Notes Offering
summary: GRAND RAPIDS, Mich.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Northpointe Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: NPB) (“Northpointe” or “Company”), the holding company for…...
body_text: Northpointe Bancshares, Inc. Announces Completion of $70 Million Subordinated Notes Offering December 09, 2025 4:30 pm EST Download as PDF GRAND RAPIDS, Mich.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Northpointe Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: NPB) (“Northpointe” or “Company”), the holding company for Northpointe Bank, today announced the completion of a private placement of $70,000,000 in aggregate principal amount of 7.50% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due 2035 (the “Notes”). Northpointe intends to use the net proceeds of the private placement to redeem its existing 8.25% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series A (the “Series A Preferred Stock”), and has notified the holders of the Series A Preferred Stock that Northpointe will be redeeming 100% of the Series A Preferred Stock effective December 30, 2025. The Notes will initially bear interest at a fixed interest rate of 7.50% per annum until December 15, 2030, with interest during this period payable semi-annually in arrears beginning June 15, 2026. From December 15, 2030, to the stated maturity date or early redemption date, the interest rate will reset quarterly to an annual floating rate equal to a benchmark rate, which is expected to be the then current Three-Month Term Secured Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”) plus 424 basis points, with interest during this period payable in arrears beginning December 15, 2030. The Notes are redeemable by the Company, in whole or in part, on any interest payment date on or after December 15, 2030, and at any time upon the occurrence of certain events. The Notes have been structured to qualify as Tier 2 capital for Northpointe for regulatory capital purposes. Piper Sandler & Co. acted as lead placement agent and Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, A Stifel Company acted as co-placement agent for the transaction, both of which were represented by Holland & Knight LLP. Alston & Bird LLP served as legal counsel to Northpointe.
